objetivo: For the student to describe the path food takes through the digestive system and the function of its main organs (mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine).
hatsumon: What happens to food after you swallow it?

turnos.utterance_formal: Today we're going to find out what happens to food once it enters our body.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Today we're going to find out what happens to food once it enters our body.

operations.text: The Digestive System

turnos.utterance_formal: Take out your notebooks and leave some room — we're going to follow the whole path.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Take out your notebooks and leave me some room, okay, 'cause we're gonna follow the whole path.

turnos.utterance_formal: Think about this: when you swallow a bite of food, where does it go and what happens to it next?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, think about it: when you swallow a bite, where does it go and what happens to it after that?

turnos.utterance_formal: Has anyone's stomach ever growled from hunger? That's part of this too.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Has anyone's stomach ever growled from hunger?... yeah, that's part of this too.

turnos.utterance_formal: When we eat, the body doesn't use food just as it is: first it has to break it down.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: When we eat, the body doesn't just use food as-is: it has to break it down first.

operations.text: Digestion
The body **breaks down** food to make use of it.

turnos.utterance_formal: The job of breaking down food is done by the digestive system.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That job of breaking down food, that's done by the digestive system.

set.text: The body **breaks down** food to make use of it. The **digestive system**, a set of organs, does this job.

turnos.utterance_formal: Digesting is exactly that: breaking food down into very small pieces.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Digesting is just that: breaking food down into teeny tiny little pieces.

set.text: The body **breaks down** food to make use of it. The **digestive system**, a set of organs, does this job. Digesting means breaking food into very small pieces.

turnos.utterance_formal: Let's picture our body here, facing us, so we can locate each organ.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Let's picture our body here, facing us, so we can find each organ.

turnos.utterance_formal: The digestive system is like a very long tube that runs through the whole body.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The digestive system is like one long ol' tube that runs through the whole body.

operations.text: The digestive system is like a very long tube running through the whole body.

turnos.utterance_formal: We're going to follow that tube from top to bottom, without skipping anything.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: We're going to follow that tube from top to bottom, without skipping anything.

turnos.utterance_formal: The food's journey starts in the mouth.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The food's journey starts in the mouth.

operations.text: Mouth and esophagus
The food's journey begins in the **mouth**.

turnos.utterance_formal: In the mouth, the teeth grind food into smaller pieces.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: In the mouth, the teeth grind food into smaller little pieces.

set.text: The food's journey begins in the **mouth**. The teeth grind food into smaller pieces.

turnos.utterance_formal: And saliva softens it and moistens it so we can swallow it.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And sa liva softens it and gets it wet so we can swallow it.

set.text: The food's journey begins in the **mouth**. The teeth grind food into smaller pieces. **Saliva** softens the food so we can swallow it.

turnos.utterance_formal: That's why I always tell you to chew slowly: that's where it all begins.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's why I always tell you guys to chew nice and slow: that's where it all starts.

operations.text: **Chewing** slowly helps, because digestion starts here.

turnos.utterance_formal: After you swallow, food goes down a tube called the esophagus.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: After you swallow, the food goes down a tube called the e sophagus.

operations.text: After swallowing, food goes down a **tube** called the esophagus, which carries it to the stomach.

turnos.utterance_formal: The esophagus pushes it downward, even if we're upside down.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The e sophagus pushes it on down, even if we're upside down, right?

operations.text: The esophagus pushes the food downward, even if we are upside down.

turnos.utterance_formal: The tube empties into the stomach, a pouch that receives everything we ate.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The tube empties out into the sto mach, a pouch that receives everything we ate.

operations.text: The stomach
The tube empties into the **stomach**, a pouch that receives everything we ate.

turnos.utterance_formal: That squeezing push that moves the food along is called peristalsis.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That squeezing push that moves the food along is called peristal sis.

operations.text: peristalsis

turnos.utterance_formal: Here it is, roughly at belly height.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Here it is, roughly around tummy height.

turnos.utterance_formal: In the stomach, very strong juices break food down until it becomes a mushy paste.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: In the sto mach, real strong juices break the food down till it's like mushy paste.

operations.text: Strong **juices** break food down until it becomes a mushy paste.

turnos.utterance_formal: It sounds gross, but it's exactly what the body needs to keep going.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Sounds gross, but it's exactly what the body needs to keep on going.

set.text: Strong **juices** break food down until it becomes a mushy paste. Gross as it sounds, the body needs it to keep going.

turnos.utterance_formal: So far we've covered three parts: the mouth, the esophagus, and the stomach.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So far we got three parts: the mouth, the e sophagus, and the sto mach.

turnos.utterance_formal: From there the paste moves into the small intestine, a very long, coiled-up tube.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: From there the mush moves into the small in testine, a real long tube all coiled up.

operations.text: The intestines
From the stomach, the paste moves into the **small intestine**, a very long, coiled-up tube.

turnos.utterance_formal: Nutrients are the good part of food, and from here they pass into the blood.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: New trients are the good part of the food, and from here they pass into the blood.

set.text: From the stomach, the paste moves into the **small intestine**, a very long, coiled-up tube. **Nutrients** are absorbed here and pass into the blood.

turnos.utterance_formal: Blood carries those nutrients to the whole body. That's why we eat.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Blood carries those nutrients to the whole body. That's why we eat.

operations.text: **Blood** carries the nutrients to the whole body.

turnos.utterance_formal: What's not useful keeps going straight to the large intestine.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: What's no good just keeps on going to the large in testine.

set.text: **Blood** carries the nutrients to the whole body. What is not useful goes on to the **large intestine**.

turnos.utterance_formal: That's where what later gets expelled when we go to the bathroom is formed.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's where what later gets pushed out when we go to the bathroom gets formed.

operations.text: The large intestine collects what the body doesn't use and forms the **waste** that gets expelled.

turnos.utterance_formal: Don't laugh, it's about as natural as it gets.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Don't laugh, it's about as natural as it gets, right?

turnos.utterance_formal: Now let's put the whole path together: food enters through the mouth and goes down the esophagus.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now let's put the whole path together: food goes in through the mouth and down the e sophagus.

turnos.utterance_formal: From the esophagus it reaches the stomach, where it turns into mush.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: From the e sophagus it gets to the sto mach, where it turns to mush.

turnos.utterance_formal: From the stomach it moves to the small intestine, which keeps the good stuff.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: From the sto mach it moves to the small in testine, which keeps the good stuff.

turnos.utterance_formal: And it ends in the large intestine, which collects the waste.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And it ends up in the large in testine, which collects the waste.

turnos.utterance_formal: See how food makes a whole journey without ever going back?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: See how the food makes this whole trip and never goes back?

turnos.utterance_formal: Look at the row of arrows: mouth, stomach, and intestine, one after another.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Check out the row of little arrows: mouth, sto mach, and in testine, one after the other.

turnos.utterance_formal: Each organ hands the food to the next one, always in the same order.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Each organ hands the food over to the next one, always in the same order, see?

turnos.utterance_formal: Let's remember where it all starts and where it goes down from there.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Let's remember where it all starts and where it goes down from there.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now for the most important part: what's the point of all this work?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now here's the important part: what's the point of all this work?

operations.text: Why it matters
Digestion gives the body **energy** and nutrients from food.

turnos.utterance_formal: Without digestion, even if we ate, the body wouldn't have energy.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Without di gestion, even if we ate, the body wouldn't have any energy.

operations.text: Without **digestion**, the body wouldn't have energy.

turnos.utterance_formal: Let's remember what it's for: to give us energy and to make use of what we eat.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Let's remember what it's for: to give us energy and to make use of what we eat.

turnos.utterance_formal: Rest your hand for a moment. Are we good? Great.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Rest your hand a sec. We good?... alright, great.

turnos.utterance_formal: And since it's so important, we need to take care of it with some habits.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And since it's so important, we gotta take care of it with some hab its.

operations.text:
Chew slowly
Eat fruits and vegetables
Drink water

turnos.utterance_formal: Simple things, but they help your stomach a whole lot.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Simple stuff, but it helps your tummy a ton.

operations.text: Simple habits help your **stomach** a lot.

turnos.utterance_formal: So you don't forget, hold on to this: food travels through five organs in order.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So you don't forget, hold on to this: food travels through five organs in order.

operations.text: Food travels through 5 **organs** in order.

turnos.utterance_formal: And today's big word, the one you shouldn't forget, is digestion.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And today's biggest word, the one you shouldn't forget, is di gestion.

set.text: Food travels through 5 **organs** in order. The key word is **digestion**.

turnos.utterance_formal: Remember what the digestive system is: the set of organs that digest food.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Remember what the digestive system is: the set of organs that digest food.
